note: PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS section 7 performance targets as machine-readable assertions. The prose source of truth is that section; this file must not be more lenient than it. plan.md section 7.3 requires p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue lag, memory, database connections and recovery time to be recorded for a claim to be accepted -- the harness records all of them and FAILS when one is unavailable.
warmupNote: PHASE 48. warmup raised 20 -> 100, and the budget at 500 ms is UNCHANGED. This is a change to how the measurement is taken, not to what it must satisfy, and it is recorded here rather than made silently because it turned a failing gate green. Evidence, three independent measurements of the same request: customer-list p50 883 ms at warmup 20; p50 261 ms when the same scenario runs third, after ~210 prior requests; p50 260 ms at warmup 100. Twenty iterations against a freshly loaded 400,000-row dataset measures JIT warm-up and cold shared buffers, not the latency a user experiences. With 100 it does. The cold-start cost is real and is recorded as a known risk in the Phase 48 report rather than deleted.

globalAssertions.errorRateRationale: A smoke run tolerates ZERO failed requests. Any non-2xx means the target is not in a state where a latency number means anything, and a latency measurement taken against a failing service is a way of reporting green without measuring.
globalAssertions.telemetryRationale: memory, database connections and queue lag are part of the claim (plan.md 7.3). A run that cannot read them fails; it does not report them as unknown and pass.

telemetry.processMemory: API process working set and managed heap, sampled before and after
telemetry.databaseConnections: pg_stat_activity connections in use versus max_connections, sampled at peak and at the end
telemetry.queueLag: pending outbox_events count and the age of the oldest pending row, plus the worker's reported lag from the management port when it exposes one
